insight: For Haiti, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally been a positive turning point, with the team gaining momentum in 5 out of 6 breaks, resulting in an average increase of 0.133 minutes of possession per minute of play. This suggests that the breaks have allowed Haiti to regroup and refocus, leading to improved performance on the field. However, when Haiti was pressing before a hydration break, they struggled to maintain their momentum, losing an average of 0.400 minutes of possession per minute of play, indicating that their high-intensity approach may have left them vulnerable after the break. In contrast, when Haiti was not pressing before a break, they were able to capitalize on the pause, maintaining or increasing their momentum in all 5 instances, with an average gain of 0.240 minutes of possession per minute of play.
